title: Outcome in patients with small cell lung cancer Multicenter – Outcome in patients with small cell lung cancer – Real-world validation of the outcome in patients with small cell lung cancer after curative-intent radiotherapy as part of multimodal concepts analogous to the ADRIATIC trial
summary:
Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) has a poor prognosis. The clinical symptoms of patients with SCLC do not differ fundamentally from those of patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Typical features include development in the central airways and often a short medical history with tumor-related symptoms such as dyspnea, cough, or signs of upper respiratory congestion. A distinctive feature of small cell lung cancer is the very rapid tumor growth (division time 30 days) and the frequent occurrence of paraneoplastic syndromes, most commonly with endocrine symptoms. 

Limited disease SCLC can be treated curatively using modern radiotherapy techniques. The better the target volume can be defined, the better the further therapy can be determined in terms of quality control. Small cell carcinoma is not only found in the lungs, but also in the bladder, prostate, urethra, cervix, etc. Here, only pulmonary SCLCs will be retrospectively analyzed with regard to their recurrence and relapse patterns (if present/cause of death) depending on other known risk factors. As part of the ADRIATIC trial, immune checkpoint inhibition with durvalumab was approved for patients treated with SCLC after definitive RCT. Immune checkpoint inhibition as maintenance therapy represents a new milestone in the treatment of SCLC. This is being validated as a systemic component in a multicenter trial for risk stratification.
